previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior toe amputations was admitted for acute kidney injury with a creatinine rise from 1.7 to 2.8. The etiology was attributed to elevated tacrolimus levels, likely contributing to his recent headache and fatigue. Tacrolimus was held initially, and losartan and spironolactone were discontinued due to hyperkalemia and concerns for pre-renal injury. Renal ultrasound showed a normal transplant kidney, ruling out rejection. The patient completed a two-week course of IV antibiotics for ongoing osteomyelitis treatment, switching from ertapenem to meropenem. His kidney function improved, creatinine returned to baseline, and he was discharged home on his prior medications with follow-up plans.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old immunosupressed man with PVD, right second finger
eschar, ulcer  // r/o osteo

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar, multisequence imaging was performed of the right hand
on a 1.5 Tesla magnet.  The patient declined administration of intravenous
contrast material.

COMPARISON:  Hand radiographs from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is T1 hypointense, STIR hyperintense signal throughout the index finger
distal phalanx, compatible with acute osteomyelitis (07:11, 4:10, 5:12). There
is mild surrounding soft tissue edema. There is also marked attenuation of the
skin overlying the medial aspect of the distal phalangeal tuft (5:9). The
remainder of the marrow signal is normal.

There is mild soft tissue edema along palmar to the base of the second
metacarpal including perivascular edema along the distal branches of the
radial artery (05:49 - 51). There is also mild subcutaneous edema along the
palmar aspect of the hand at the level of the third through fifth MCP joints
(___).

There is a small quantity of fluid within the flexor tendon sheath to the long
finger at the level of the MCP joint, compatible with mild tenosynovitis
(05:38). There is an adjacent 5 mm T2 hyperintense structure, compatible with
a ganglion (05:33). The flexor tendons themselves are within normal limits.
The extensor tendons are unremarkable. The median nerve within the carpal
tunnel is grossly normal.

There is ulnar deviation of the index finger about the MCP joint. There is no
frank dislocation. A tiny well corticated ossified body along the lateral
aspect of the long finger proximal phalangeal base likely relates to remote
trauma (6:5).

IMPRESSION:


1. Findings compatible with acute osteomyelitis involving the index finger
distal phalanx. Marked attenuation of the skin overlying the medial aspect of
the distal phalangeal tuft should be correlated clinically for evidence of
ulceration.
2. Mild soft tissue edema along the palmar aspect of the hand at the level of
the MCP joints with extension along the distal branches of the radial artery,
likely reactive.
3. Mild tenosynovitis of the long finger flexor tendon. Tiny adjacent ganglion
along the palmar aspect of the third MCP joint.
